title: The Goat and the Vine
summary: A mischievous goat pushed through a broken garden fence and began gnawing the tender shoots and green bark of a young, flourishing grapevine, chewing down to the white wood....
full_text:
A mischievous goat pushed through a broken garden fence and began gnawing the tender shoots and green bark of a young, flourishing grapevine, chewing down to the white wood.

The wounded vine wept bitter sap upon the earth and whispered:

"Chew on, merciless beast! Strip my bark and devour my green leaves! Yet my roots run deep in the soil, and when the autumn harvest arrives, I will still yield enough wine to pour libations over your altar when you are sacrificed!"
moral: Those who maliciously destroy the fruit of the earth will face righteous retribution.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Goat and the Vine"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.

author: Aesop (~620–564 BCE / Trans. George Fyler Townsend)
